  ## The strongest architecture idea I would try now                            
                                                                                
  ### **Target–Background Residual Fusion (TBRF)**                              
                                                                                
  This is the one I think is substantially more sensible than CER/replay/class  
  weighting.                                                                    
                                                                                
  Your measured polarity failure is:                                            
                                                                                
  * POS → NEU: 86                                                               
  * NEG → NEU: 35                                                               
  * NEU → POS: 45                                                               
                                                                                
  with NEU recall already 89.46%.                                               
                                                                                
  That strongly suggests the model often falls back to the **overall tweet      
  sentiment** instead of the sentiment of the target aspect.                    
                                                                                
  The current TARKAN representation is essentially:                             
                                                                                
  [                                                                             
  z = KAN(t_k,\tilde v_k,\tilde g_k)                                            
  ]                                                                             
                                                                                
  where (t_k) is the aspect representation and the visual/KG evidence are fused 
  into it.                                                                      
                                                                                
  The architectural change:                                                     
                                                                                
  ### 1. Build two text representations                                         
                                                                                
  For an aspect (a_k):                                                          
                                                                                
  [                                                                             
  t_{local} = \text{AttnPool}(H_{\text{aspect context}})                        
  ]                                                                             
                                                                                
  and                                                                           
                                                                                
  [                                                                             
  t_{global} = \text{AttnPool}(H_{\text{tweet}})                                
  ]                                                                             
                                                                                
  Then explicitly form:                                                         
                                                                                
  [                                                                             
  \Delta_t=t_{local}-t_{global}.                                                
  ]                                                                             
                                                                                
  Now KAN receives:                                                             
                                                                                
  [                                                                             
  z =                                                                           
  KAN(                                                                          
  [t_{local},\Delta_t],                                                         
  \tilde v_k,                                                                   
  \tilde g_k                                                                    
  ).                                                                            
  ]                                                                             
                                                                                
  So the model is no longer only asking:                                        
                                                                                
  > “What does this tweet say about this aspect?”                               
                                                                                
  It is structurally encouraged to learn:                                       
                                                                                
  > **“What is different about this aspect compared with the overall tone of    
  the tweet?”**                                                                 
                                                                                
  That is exactly the direction your POS/NEG→NEU failure points toward.         
                                                                                
  ### Why this is different from the things you already killed                  
                                                                                
  You already tried:                                                            
                                                                                
  * sibling marking,                                                            
  * sibling-logit loss,                                                         
  * SupCon,                                                                     
  * class weighting,                                                            
  * minority margins,                                                           
  * reliability gating,                                                         
  * extra combiners.                                                            
                                                                                
  Those manipulate inputs, losses, or decisions.                                
                                                                                
  **TBRF changes the representation that reaches KAN.**                         
                                                                                
  And it adds only a tiny amount of computation.                                
                                                                                
  ---                                                                           
                                                                                
  # Even better: make the residual evidence-aware                               
                                                                                
  I would actually make the architecture:                                       
                                                                                
  ```text                                                                       
                    H_tweet                                                     
                       │                                                        
            ┌──────────┴──────────┐                                             
            ↓                     ↓                                             
       t_global              t_aspect                                           
                                  │                                             
                                  ↓                                             
                       Δ_text = t_aspect - t_global                             
                                  │                                             
         ┌────────────────────────┼─────────────────────┐                       
         │                        │                     │                       
         ↓                        ↓                     ↓                       
     Δ_text                    visual                 KG                        
                                evidence              evidence                  
         │                        │                     │                       
         └────────────────────────┴─────────────────────┘                       
                                  ↓                                             
                                KAN                                             
                                  ↓                                             
                           ASC / polarity                                       
  ```                                                                           
                                                                                
  This is **TARKAN-native** because you're still doing exactly what TARKAN      
  claims to do: fuse the aspect representation with relevance-filtered visual   
  evidence and KG evidence through KAN.                                         
                                                                                
  You're simply giving KAN a much more useful aspect signal.                    
                                                                                
  ---                                                                           
                                                                                
  # Second architecture I would seriously test                                  
                                                                                
  ## **Aspect–Evidence Cross-Attention before KAN**                             
                                                                                
  Right now the aspect is compressed into (t_k), visual evidence into (\tilde   
  v_k), KG into (\tilde g_k), and then KAN fuses them.                          
                                                                                
  That can lose the **specific relation** between an aspect and its evidence.   
                                                                                
  Instead:                                                                      
                                                                                
  [                                                                             
  Q=W_q t_k                                                                     
  ]                                                                             
                                                                                
  and let the aspect query the evidence tokens:                                 
                                                                                
  [                                                                             
  E_k=[H_t^{local},\tilde V_k,\tilde G_k]                                       
  ]                                                                             
                                                                                
  [                                                                             
  A_k=\text{softmax}(QK_E^T/\sqrt d)                                            
  ]                                                                             
                                                                                
  [                                                                             
  e_k=A_kV_E.                                                                   
  ]                                                                             
                                                                                
  Then:                                                                         
                                                                                
  [                                                                             
  z_k=KAN(t_k,e_k,\tilde v_k,\tilde g_k).                                       
  ]                                                                             
                                                                                
  So rather than:                                                               
                                                                                
  ```text                                                                       
  aspect + evidence → generic fusion                                            
  ```                                                                           
                                                                                
  you get:                                                                      
                                                                                
  ```text                                                                       
  aspect                                                                        
     ↓ query                                                                    
  which evidence actually matters?                                              
     ↓                                                                          
  evidence-conditioned aspect representation                                    
     ↓                                                                          
  KAN                                                                           
  ```                                                                           
                                                                                
  This is only **one small cross-attention block**.                             
                                                                                
  It preserves every major TARKAN component.                                    
                                                                                
  ---                                                                           
                                                                                
  # Third: **Tri-Interaction KAN**                                              
                                                                                
  Your present KAN effectively combines modality representations.               
                                                                                
  A more powerful but still small change is to explicitly include **pairwise    
  interactions**:                                                               
                                                                                
  [                                                                             
  x =                                                                           
  [                                                                             
  t,\ v,\ g,                                                                    
  t\odot v,                                                                     
  t\odot g,                                                                     
  v\odot g                                                                      
  ].                                                                            
  ]                                                                             
                                                                                
  Then project back to 768 and give that to KAN.                                
                                                                                
  The important terms are:                                                      
                                                                                
  [                                                                             
  t\odot v                                                                      
  ]                                                                             
                                                                                
  meaning:                                                                      
                                                                                
  > visual evidence **conditioned on the aspect**                               
                                                                                
  and                                                                           
                                                                                
  [                                                                             
  t\odot g                                                                      
  ]                                                                             
                                                                                
  meaning:                                                                      
                                                                                
  > KG evidence **conditioned on the aspect**.                                  
                                                                                
  That is more expressive than simply handing KAN three independent vectors.    
                                                                                
  This is especially attractive because your central TARKAN premise is          
  **aspect-conditioned evidence selection**. The architecture should therefore  
  explicitly represent *aspect × evidence interactions*, rather than hope KAN   
  discovers all of them from concatenated modality states.                      
                                                                                
  ---                                                                           
                                                                                
  # What I would NOT do now                                                     
                                                                                
  I would stop spending time on:                                                
                                                                                
  ```text                                                                       
  ❌ another ensemble                                                           
  ❌ another combiner                                                           
  ❌ another confidence selector                                                
  ❌ replay / CER / RER                                                         
  ❌ class weighting                                                            
  ❌ another POS-vs-NEU margin                                                  
  ❌ another 7B member                                                          
  ❌ annotation-policy head                                                     
  ```                                                                           
                                                                                
  Your newest results already give us reasons to stop.                          
                                                                                
  CER's apparent +0.58 on t2015 disappeared on independent t2017, with a        
  three-tower mean of only +0.02.                                               
                                                                                
  And your existing member-selection machinery has repeatedly failed to turn    
  additional predictions into stable gains.                                     
                                                                                
  ---                                                                           
                                                                                
  # The experiment I would run first                                            
                                                                                
  **TBRF only. Nothing else changed.**                                          
                                                                                
  Baseline:                                                                     
                                                                                
  ```text                                                                       
  BERTweet                                                                      
  + CLIP                                                                        
  + anchor generator                                                            
  + teacher relevance                                                           
  + teacher KG filtering                                                        
  + KAN                                                                         
  + ASC                                                                         
  ```                                                                           
                                                                                
  New:                                                                          
                                                                                
  ```text                                                                       
  same exact model                                                              
  +                                                                             
  t_local                                                                       
  +                                                                             
  t_global                                                                      
  +                                                                             
  Δ_text = t_local - t_global                                                   
  ```                                                                           
                                                                                
  Then KAN.                                                                     
                                                                                
  No special labels.                                                            
                                                                                
  No t2017 training.                                                            
                                                                                
  No extra teacher calls.                                                       
                                                                                
  No additional model.                                                          
                                                                                
  No benchmark-specific annotation head.                                        
                                                                                
  ### One crucial implementation detail                                         
                                                                                
  Do **not** use a crude ±4-token window as `t_local`.                          
                                                                                
  Use the **aspect-conditioned attention** over all tweet tokens, with a        
  positional bias centered on the aspect span.                                  
                                                                                
  That gives the model the freedom to use:                                      
                                                                                
  * nearby opinion words,                                                       
  * negations,                                                                  
  * modifiers,                                                                  
  * long-distance dependencies,                                                 
                                                                                
  without forcing the sentiment signal into a fixed window.                     
                                                                                
  ---                                                                           
                                                                                
  ## My ranking now                                                             
                                                                                
  | Architecture                        | TARKAN faithful | Cost | Why I'd try  
  it                                   |                                        
  | ----------------------------------- | --------------: | ---: |              
  ------------------------------------------------ |                            
  | **TBRF: target − tweet residual**   |               ✅ |  Low | Directly    
  attacks POS/NEG→NEU/global-tone failure |                                     
  | **Aspect→Evidence cross-attention** |               ✅ |  Low | Makes       
  evidence genuinely aspect-conditioned      |                                  
  | **Tri-interaction KAN**             |               ✅ |  Low | Explicit    
  aspect×visual×KG interactions           |                                     
  | Annotation-policy head              |              ⚠️ |  Low |              
  Benchmark-specific; I would reject it            |                            
  | CER/RER                             | ❌ as SOTA route |  Low | Independent 
  validation killed the apparent gain  |                                        
                                                                                
  And importantly, **none of these changes TARKAN's identity**. The original    
  inference still computes the predicted aspect, relevance-filtered visual      
  evidence, filtered KG representation, KAN fusion, and polarity from the       
  student alone.                                                                
                                                                                
  **TBRF is the one I'd run first.** It is the cleanest architecture-level      
  response to the actual error pattern you've measured, rather than another     
  attempt to manipulate noisy labels or ensemble votes.                         
  }

● Built and smoke-testing. Explaining the design choice that decides whether
  this is real:

  Both heads read the same word representations. The anchor emissions come from
  proj(hw); the polarity comes from span-pooled hw. The joint margin — U(gold, 
  y*) > U(hard_negative, ŷ) + m with U = A(s) · P(ŷ|s)^λ — is differentiable
  through both, so it backprops into hw itself. That is the difference from
  D.2's frozen selector: it can make "is this span's polarity determinable" part
  of what the candidate state encodes, rather than combining two fixed scores.

  Two disciplines carried over from what actually worked here:

  - alpha is zero-initialised on the polarity→emissions feedback, so training
  starts at exactly an ordinary decoupled tagger and any coupling must be
  earned. That's the §C.27 discipline that made the PDS residual work where
  representation-matching failed.
  - Hard negatives are boundary errors (s±1, e±1) around gold spans — the
  mistakes the anchor head actually makes — not random tokens.

  The gate is a_selected, and I've made the code print it against 80.52 
  explicitly. A move to 82+ is above the ±1.31 detection floor and is the claim.
  If PACS merely reproduces the post-hoc product it lands near 70.8 joint with
  a_selected unchanged — and that's the falsification, not a tuning problem.

  Two things I'm not doing: no t2017 (t2015 only, per your direction —
  validation will be paired seeds), and no single-run verdict.

● Smoke test runs end-to-end (2 epochs, so the low numbers are expected — MATE
  needs 9–11 epochs to converge). But it exposed a real bug: alpha sits at
  exactly +0.000 after two epochs, and it can never move.

  alpha is initialised to 0 and fb is zero-initialised. So fb(·) = 0, hence
  ∂loss/∂alpha = fb · ∂loss/∂emis = 0; and ∂loss/∂fb = alpha · (…) = 0. Both 
  parameters have identically zero gradient forever — a double-zero-init 
  deadlock. The entire feedback branch is dead code that would have silently
  contributed nothing.

  There's a second problem I should have caught when writing it: the feedback is
  applied only to gold spans in training and not at all in infer() — a
  train/test mismatch. Rather than patch two entangled mechanisms, I'm removing
  the feedback branch: the joint margin is the actual coupling, since U = 
  A(s)·P(ŷ|s)^λ is differentiable through both heads that share hw.

  hypothesis.

  The cause is in my code:

  lj = torch.relu(args.margin + Un.mean() - Ug.mean())

  That compares the batch mean of gold utilities against the batch mean of
  negatives — one scalar constraint per batch, trivially satisfied once gold
  spans generally outscore boundary errors. A hard-negative margin has to be per
  gold span against its own negatives, or it isn't a hard-negative loss at all.

● Both critiques are correct, and the first one contradicts something I
  established myself.

  1. I used OOF failure as a ground-truth label, which D.11 says it isn't.
  D.11's whole finding is that the residual errors are consensus errors — the
  family is confidently wrong together. So "0 of 4 towers correct" means "these
  four models share a blind spot," not "this polarity is unknowable." I wrote
  that finding and then built a loss that treats the same signal as intrinsic
  difficulty. That's self-contradictory, and it matters: the loss as written
  teaches the extractor to avoid what our current classifiers are bad at, which
  inflates joint F1 by refusing hard cases rather than solving them.

  2. The cost argument assumed P(wrong) = 1. Correct. The real rule is extract 
  iff q > 0.5, since expected error is 2(1−q) for extract vs 1 for skip. With
  smoothing, q̂ = (k+α)/(4+2α) gives a signed utility u = 2q−1: k=0 → −0.67, k=2 
  → 0, k=4 → +0.67. My d = k/4 ∈ [0,1] ranking has no 0.5 crossover at all — it
  just orders spans, so it pushes k=2 spans down when they should be neutral.

  3. The control caveat is real, and it has a consequence neither of us stated:
  the shared encoder gives MATE 84.83 vs the dedicated 85.77–87.01. So PACS as a
  standalone system starts ~5 points below the ensemble at 65.24 and cannot
  plausibly reach 72.9 alone. Its realistic value is as a better-ranked 
  candidate source feeding the existing 19-member MASC — that's the integration
  I'll test if the ablation shows signal.

  Switching d = k/4 to u = 2q−1 changes nothing in a pairwise ranking loss — u

  real content of the q > 0.5 insight is an absolute threshold: spans with q < 
  0.5 must be actively suppressed, not merely ranked lower. That needs an
  absolute target, which my pairwise form doesn't have.

● Three real issues, all fixed. Being precise about each, including one where
  the proposed fix does less than it appears:

  1. I contradicted my own D.11. I used OOF-family failure as a ground-truth
  "indeterminable" label — but D.11's finding is that the residual errors are
  consensus errors, so 0-of-4 towers wrong means those four correlated models
  share a blind spot, not that the polarity is unknowable. q is now
  Laplace-smoothed, q̂ = (k+α)/(4+2α), so it stays an estimate rather than an
  assertion.

  2. The q > 0.5 correction is right, but not where it looks. Switching d = k/4
  → u = 2q−1 changes nothing in a pairwise ranking loss — u is a monotone affine
  transform of d, so the ordering is identical. The real content is an absolute
  threshold, which my pairwise form never had:

  ┌────────────┬───────┬─────────────┬──────────┐
  │ k/4 towers │ old d │ corrected u │  action  │
  ├────────────┼───────┼─────────────┼──────────┤
  │ 0          │ 0.00  │ −0.67       │ suppress │
  ├────────────┼───────┼─────────────┼──────────┤
  │ 2          │ 0.50  │ +0.00       │ neutral  │
  ├────────────┼───────┼─────────────┼──────────┤
  │ 4          │ 1.00  │ +0.67       │ boost    │
  └────────────┴───────┴─────────────┴──────────┘

  The old ranking pushed k=2 spans down as "below average"; the algebra says
  they're exactly indifferent. That's the substantive fix.

  3. My gate couldn't measure the claim. a_selected alone can't show
  anti-correlation. It now also reports a_gold and prints a_selected − a_gold —
  the decoupled pipeline's is −0.68, and PACS succeeds only if that turns
  positive without wrecking MATE.

  One consequence neither of us drew. The shared encoder already costs
  extraction (MATE 84.83 vs dedicated 85.77–87.01), so PACS as a standalone
  system starts at joint 65.24 and cannot plausibly reach 72.9 alone — no
  coupling gain closes 5+ points. Its realistic value is as a better-ranked
  candidate source feeding the existing 19-member MASC ensemble. That's the
  integration I'll test if the ablation shows signal, and it also means the
  two-encoder redesign isn't worth building until then.

  I'm letting the rank arm finish as the ablation it was launched as — it
  answers whether "prefer polarity-solvable aspects" carries any signal at all,
  which gates everything downstream.

  One warning                                                                   
                                                                                
  The screenshot says q=(k+α)/(4+2α) and seems to use the four OOF towers.      
  That's fine as a very crude estimator, but four votes is tiny.                
                                                                                
  For example, with smoothing, k=2 is treated as essentially neutral. But k=2   
  doesn't mean the candidate has exactly 50% probability of correct polarity;   
  the four models can be highly correlated—which your D11 result says they are. 
                                                                                
  So I would treat q as a ranking/heuristic signal, not a calibrated            
  probability.                                                                  
                                                                                
  If the experiment produces a positive result, the next version should         
  probably use OOF probability averaging from the actual member softmaxes, not  
  just k/4.                                                                     
                                                                                
  Bottom line                                                                   
                                                                                
  The current correction is going in the right direction.                       
                                                                                
  The bad version was:                                                          
                                                                                
  “four models failed → this example is intrinsically unknowable → train MATE   
  to avoid it.”                                                                 
                                                                                
  The corrected version is:                                                     
                                                                                
  “four models failed → this is estimated low-confidence downstream polarity →  
  test whether that signal can improve candidate selection.”                    
                                                                                
  That is a legitimate hypothesis.                                              
                                                                                
  And letting the current rank arm finish is exactly right. Don't modify it     
  again mid-run. The result will tell us whether “polarity-solvable candidates  
  should be preferentially extracted” contains any real signal at all.

  reference: 0.659).

  from two towers and predicting whether two different architectures get it

  difficulty is a largely model-independent property — not merely the shared
  blind spot D.11 warned about. That's what makes the direction viable at all.

  survives prediction.

  One place I'd push back on their plan: they framed this as a PACS diagnostic.
  But PACS starts at joint 65.24 because of shared-encoder negative transfer, so
  it can't reach 72.9 as a standalone system no matter how well the coupling
  works. The direct test — train P(pair correct) from text, use it to filter the
  existing 19-member ensemble — measures the same hypothesis, avoids the
  negative transfer entirely, and costs 15 min instead of 50. That's queued
  behind the PACS ablation, which I'm letting finish as they advised.

  compromise between tagging and difficulty-estimation.

  And the mechanism that unifies them:

  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┬───────┐
  │                 source of q                 │  AUC  │
  ├─────────────────────────────────────────────┼───────┤
  │ other classifiers + the gold labels         │ 0.906 │
  ├─────────────────────────────────────────────┼───────┤
  │ geometric product                           │ 0.733 │
  ├─────────────────────────────────────────────┼───────┤
  │ a model reading the text                    │ 0.705 │
  ├─────────────────────────────────────────────┼───────┤
  │ the same ensemble's disagreement, no labels │ 0.650 │
  └─────────────────────────────────────────────┴───────┘

  q is a property of model competence, not a readable property of the input.
  Strip the labels and the ensemble's own disagreement carries 0.650 — barely
  above MASC confidence. So the 74.68 oracle was never a target: the information
  that would fix the selection only exists once you already know the answer.
  That's the deepest statement of the D.2 ceiling, and it reconciles with D.11
  rather than contradicting it — the residual errors are consensus errors, and
  the consensus cannot identify which of its own answers are wrong.

  Two things worth flagging about process. Both PACS bugs — the double-zero-init
  dead branch and the batch-mean margin the control had already satisfied at
  0.0000 — would have produced a plausible null attributed to the hypothesis.
  Both were caught by printing intermediate quantities rather than reading the
  final metric. Given D.20's ±1.31 floor, that's the only defence available.

  And the threshold correction was real but pointed the wrong way for us: q > 
  0.5 minimises error count; micro-F1 wants q < F1/2 = 0.353.

  Standing result unchanged: 70.32 choice-free / 70.62 dev-selected, 15 of 19
  baselines cleared. Everything committed and pushed; GPU idle.

       51 -## Measured negatives (do not re-run these)                   
       52 -| lever | test | vs 70.37 |                                   
       10 +§C.18 is the sharpest structural finding in the project:      
       11 +                                                              
       12 +| MASC accuracy measured on | value |                         
       13 +|---|---|                                                     
       14 +| all gold spans (`a_gold`) | **81.20** |                     
       15 +| spans MATE actually extracts (`a_selected`) | **80.52** |   
       16 +| spans MATE **misses** | **86.73** |                         
       17 +                                                              
       18 +The extractor systematically selects the spans its own classif
          +ier is **worst** at. The                                      
       19 +anti-correlation is `a_selected − a_gold = −0.68`. MADSC's pub
          +lished numbers imply the                                      
       20 +opposite sign (`a` 84.18 against 82.34 gold-span, i.e. **+1.84
          +**) — a ~2.5-point swing in                                   
       21 +`a`, almost exactly our joint gap.                            
       22 +                                                              
       23 +The cause is structural and self-inflicted: Chapters C/D delib
          +erately built MATE and MASC as                                
       24 +*decorrelated* model families, which is ideal for ensembling a
          +nd exactly wrong for joint                                    
       25 +MABSA.                                                        
       26 +                                                              
       27 +**Why this reframed the target.** The bar had been read as "ge
          +t `a` to 83.1 on all gold                                     
       28 +spans", which is above every published number. But spans at **
          +86.73** accuracy already exist                                
       29 +in this system — they are simply not selected. Holding MATE@τ 
          +at 87.8, moving `a_selected`                                  
       30 +from 80.4 to ~83.5 clears 72.9. That is a selection problem in
          +side a population we already                                  
       31 +have, not a demand for SOTA polarity.

       34 +                                                              
       35 +## 2. The arithmetic — including a threshold error worth recor
          +ding                                                          
       36 +                                                              
       37 +Micro-F1 is `2·TP/(|pred| + |gold|)`. Dropping a prediction wh
          +ose probability of being                                      
       38 +correct is `q` therefore improves F1 exactly when             
       39 +                                                              
       40 +```                                                           
       41 +q < F1/2          (derivation: 2(TP−q)/(K−1+G) > 2TP/(K+G)  ⇔ 
          + q < TP/(K+G) = F1/2)                                         
       42 +```                                                           
       43 +                                                              
       44 +which is **0.353** at our operating point (TP 728, kept 1032, 
          +gold 1037, F1 70.6).                                          
       45 +                                                              
       46 +**Both I and the ChatGPT proposal initially used `q > 0.5`.** 
          +That rule minimises *expected                                 
       47 +error count* (`2(1−q)` if extracted vs `1` if skipped) — a dif
          +ferent objective — and it                                     
       48 +over-drops. With **oracle** knowledge of `q`:                 
       49 +                                                              
       50 +| cut | predictions dropped | TP lost | projected F1 |        
       51 +|---|---|---|---|                                             
       52 +| **q < 0.353** (correct for F1) | 187 | 25.2 | **74.68** |   
       53 +| q < 0.40 | 205 | 32.1 | 74.66 |                             
       54 +| q < 0.50 (the intuitive rule) | 253 | 53.6 | 74.28 |        
       55 +                                                              
       56 +**74.68 clears the 72.9 bar.** Everything that follows is abou
          +t whether `q` is obtainable                                   
       57 +without the answers.                                          
       58 +                                                              
       59 +---                                                           
       60 +                                                              
       61 +## 3. The determinability signal `q`, and its validation      
       62 +                                                              
       63 +`q` = probability that a candidate's polarity will be predicte
          +d correctly, estimated from                                   
       64 +four architecturally distinct out-of-fold towers (`oof_btwL`, 
          +`oof_btw`, `oof_deb`,                                         
       65 +`oof_twrob`).                                                 
       66 +                                                              
       67 +**Estimator choice, measured not assumed.** Vote-counting (`k/
          +4`) throws away most of the                                   
       68 +signal — within the k=2 bucket the true `q` spans 0.29–0.71:  
       69 +                                                              
       70 +| k of 4 towers correct | n | `q` range | mean `q` |          
       71 +|---|---|---|---|                                             
       72 +| 0 | 356 | 0.00–0.35 | 0.055 |                               
       73 +| 1 | 278 | 0.13–0.50 | 0.297 |                               
       74 +| 2 | 303 | 0.29–0.71 | 0.508 |                               
       75 +| 3 | 462 | 0.43–0.86 | 0.717 |                               
       76 +| 4 | 1780 | 0.68–1.00 | 0.961 |                              
       77 +                                                              
       78 +**Cross-family transfer test.** Estimate `q` from 2 towers, th
          +en predict whether the *other*                                
       79 +2 architectures get the same aspect right:                    
       80 +                                                              
       81 +| q from | predicts | AUC (vote count) | AUC (mean softmax) | 
       82 +|---|---|---|---|                                             
       83 +| btwL+btw | deb+twrob | 0.8744 | **0.9217** |                
       84 +| btwL+deb | btw+twrob | 0.8439 | 0.9022 |                    
       85 +| btwL+twrob | btw+deb | 0.8533 | 0.9028 |                    
       86 +| btw+deb | btwL+twrob | 0.8554 | 0.9049 |                    
       87 +| btw+twrob | btwL+deb | 0.8454 | 0.9023 |                    
       88 +| deb+twrob | btwL+btw | 0.8547 | 0.9046 |                    
       89 +| **mean** | | **0.8545** | **0.9064** |                      
       90 +                                                              
       91 +So per-example polarity difficulty is a largely **model-indepe
          +ndent** property of examples —                                
       92 +**not** merely the shared blind spot §D.11 warned about — and 
          +the softmax estimator is worth                                
       93 +**+0.05 AUC** over vote-counting. Reference: §D.2 measured MAS
          +C max-probability at AUC                                      
       94 +**0.659** for the same target.                                
       95 +                                                              
       96 +`q` is saved in `data/qdet_train.npz` (3179 aspects). 779 (24.
          +5%) fall below 0.5; 576                                       
       97 +(18.1%) below the correct 0.353 cut.                          
       98 +

      100 +                                                              
      101 +## 4. PACS itself — architecture and results                  
      102 +                                                              
      103 +`experts/pacs.py`. One encoder, two heads:                    
      104 +                                                              
      105 +```                                                           
      106 +deberta-v3-large ─► word representations hw                   
      107 +                      ├── proj → BIO emissions → linear-chain 
          +CRF   (anchor / MATE)                                         
      108 +                      └── span pooling [mean, first, last] → M
          +LP    (polarity / MASC)                                       
      109 +                                                              
      110 +  U(s) = A(s) · P(ŷ|s)^λ          A(s) = mean(1 − P(O)) over t
          +he span                                                       
      111 +```                                                           
      112 +                                                              
      113 +Both heads read the **same** `hw`, so a joint loss backprops t
          +hrough both at once — which is                                
      114 +what a post-hoc product over frozen scores structurally cannot
          + do. TARKAN's identity is                                     
      115 +preserved: BIO anchor generation with a CRF, aspect-conditione
          +d polarity, student-only                                      
      116 +inference.                                                    
      117 +                                                              
      118 +### Results (seed 42, 16 epochs, identical recipe throughout) 
      119 +                                                              
      120 +| arm | MATE@τ dev | MATE@τ test | `a_selected` dev | **`a_sel
          +ected` test** | joint dev | **joint test** |                  
      121 +|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|                                 
      122 +| **control** (`lam_joint` 0, `lam_det` 0) | 84.70 | 84.83 | 7
          +8.88 | **76.91** | 66.82 | **65.24** |                        
      123 +| **determinability-ranked** (`lam_det` 1.0) | 84.96 | 85.17 |
          + 77.60 | **74.00** | 65.93 | **63.02** |                      
      124 +| Δ | +0.26 | +0.34 | −1.28 | **−2.91** | −0.89 | **−2.22** | 
      125 +                                                              
      126 +**The result is negative and of the opposite sign to the hypot
          +hesis.** Training the extractor                               
      127 +to prefer polarity-determinable spans made its selected spans 
          +**harder** for its own                                        
      128 +classifier (`a_selected` −2.91) and cost 2.22 joint F1. At −2.
          +22 this is well clear of the                                  
      129 +§D.20 ±1.31 single-pair detection floor, so it is a real degra
          +dation rather than noise.                                     
      130 +                                                              
      131 +Reading: forcing the anchor score to encode difficulty **fight
          +s the tagging objective** and                                 
      132 +damages both. MATE@τ rose slightly (+0.34) while the polarity 
          +of what it selected collapsed.                                
      133 +                                                              
      134 +### A structural limit found while designing the control      
      135 +Hard parameter sharing costs extraction before PACS even start
          +s: the shared-encoder control                                 
      136 +gets MATE@τ **84.83** against the dedicated tagger's **85.77**
          + and the 5-member ensemble's                                  
      137 +**87.01**. PACS therefore begins at joint 65.24 and **cannot b
          +e a standalone system** — no                                  
      138 +coupling gain closes 5+ points to the 70.4 ensemble. Its only 
          +plausible use was as a                                        
      139 +better-ranked *candidate source*, which §5–6 then tested direc
          +tly and more cheaply.                                         
      140 +

      142 +                                                              
      143 +## 5. Two bugs found before they could fake a result          
      144 +                                                              
      145 +Both would have produced a *plausible null* attributable to th
          +e hypothesis rather than to the                               
      146 +code. Both were caught by printing intermediate quantities, no
          +t the final metric.                                           
      147 +                                                              
      148 +**(a) Double zero-init dead branch.** The first version had a 
          +polarity→emissions feedback                                   
      149 +gate with **both** the gate scalar `alpha` and its projection 
          +`fb` zero-initialised:                                        
      150 +                                                              
      151 +```                                                           
      152 +∂L/∂alpha = fb    = 0        ∂L/∂fb = alpha = 0               
      153 +```                                                           
      154 +                                                              
      155 +Both parameters had **identically zero gradient forever**. The
          + branch was dead code that                                    
      156 +looked principled and printed a plausible `alpha +0.000`. It w
          +as also applied only to gold                                  
      157 +spans during training and **never at inference** — train/test 
          +inconsistent. Removed; the                                    
      158 +joint margin is the actual coupling.                          
      159 +                                                              
      160 +**(b) Vacuous batch-mean margin.** The hard-negative loss comp
          +ared batch **means**:                                         
      161 +                                                              
      162 +```                                                           
      163 +lj = relu(margin + Un.mean() − Ug.mean())                     
      164 +```                                                           
      165 +                                                              
      166 +That is one scalar constraint per batch, which ordinary traini
          +ng already satisfies. The                                     
      167 +control arm logs the term even though `lam_joint = 0` there, a
          +nd it read **0.0013 by epoch 8                                
      168 +and 0.0000 by epoch 12 without ever being optimised.** Running
          + the coupled arm would have                                   
      169 +returned "coupling does nothing" as an artifact of the loss. R
          +eplaced with a true pairwise                                  
      170 +margin — every gold span against **its own** boundary errors, 
      171 +`relu(m + U_neg − U_gold[owner]).mean()` — verified on a live 
          +batch (15 gold spans → 45                                     
      172 +negatives, every negative owned by a gold span in the same sen
          +tence, spot-checks are genuine                                
      173 +boundary shifts).                                             
      174 +                                                              
      175 +**(c) Conceptual, also corrected.** The first formulation trea
          +ted "0 of 4 towers correct" as                                
      176 +a ground-truth *indeterminability label*, which contradicts §D
          +.11's own finding that residual                               
      177 +errors are **consensus** errors. `q` was made a Laplace-smooth
          +ed estimate,                                                  
      178 +`q̂ = (k+α)/(4+2α)`, and the loss given an absolute threshold r
          +ather than a pure ranking —                                   
      179 +noting that mapping `d = k/4` to `u = 2q−1` changes **nothing*
          +* in a pairwise ranking loss,                                 
      180 +since it is a monotone affine transform. The real content of t
          +he `q > 0.5` insight is a                                     
      181 +threshold, which the pairwise form never had.                 
      182 +

      231 +## 7. ★ The mechanism — why the 74.68 oracle is unreachable   
      232 +                                                              
      233 +| source of `q` | AUC |                                       
      234 +|---|---|                                                     
      235 +| other classifiers **compared to the gold labels** | **0.906*
          +* |                                                           
      236 +| the geometric product | 0.733 |                             
      237 +| a model reading the **text** | 0.705 |                      
      238 +| the same ensemble's **disagreement, without labels** | 0.650
          + |                                                            
      239 +                                                              
      240 +**`q` is a property of model competence, not a readable proper
          +ty of the input.** It is                                      
      241 +recoverable at 0.906 only by running independent classifiers *
          +and comparing them to the                                     
      242 +answer*. Strip the labels and the identical ensemble's disagre
          +ement carries 0.650 — barely                                  
      243 +above MASC confidence.                                        
      244 +                                                              
      245 +So **74.68 was never a target**: the information that would fi
          +x the selection exists only                                   
      246 +once you already know the answer. This is the deepest statemen
          +t of the §D.2 ceiling (a                                      
      247 +selector fitted directly on test cannot beat the honest one), 
          +and it reconciles with §D.11                                  
      248 +rather than contradicting it — the residual errors are consens
          +us errors **and** the consensus                               
      249 +cannot identify which of its own answers are the wrong ones.  
      250 +

      252 +                                                              
      253 +## 8. What this closes, and what it does not                  
      254 +                                                              
      255 +**Closed.** The extraction↔polarity coupling route, by three i
          +ndependent attacks: internalise                               
      256 +`q` in the extractor (−2.22), predict `q` from text (AUC 0.705
          + < 0.733), estimate it from                                   
      257 +member disagreement (+0.034 AUC → 0.0 F1).                    
      258 +                                                              
      259 +**Not overturned.** §C.18 remains a true and interesting obser
          +vation about the system — the                                 
      260 +extractor really does select the spans its classifier handles 
          +worst. What PACS establishes is                               
      261 +that the anti-correlation is **not actionable**, because actin
          +g on it requires a competence                                 
      262 +estimate that only the labels provide.                        
      263 +                                                              
      264 +**Standing result unchanged: 70.32** (choice-free, all correct
          + members equal-weight) /                                      
      265 +**70.62** (fixed 19-member structure). 15 of 19 t2015 baseline
          +s cleared; SGBIS 71.1,                                        
      266 +DQPSA 71.9, VLHA 72.5, MADSC 72.9 remain above.

  tested:

  α+_j ∝ exp(r_j)·σ( s_j)  →  E+     (support for positive)
  α−_j ∝ exp(r_j)·σ(−s_j)  →  E−     (support for negative)
  head ← [t_a, E+, E−, E+ − E−]

  Instead of one pooled context vector, the head gets an explicit directional 
  contrast — aimed straight at the 158 of 186 errors that are minority↔NEU. s_j
  is learned, not seeded from SenticNet, because §C14 measured that hard
  opinion-word manipulation damages the pretrained representation.

  There is one major family you still have **not really attacked**:             
                                                                                
  # Train TARKAN to learn **evidence causality**, not evidence classification   
                                                                                
  This is different from PACS, CER, TBRF, TORF, PDS, and your previous fusion   
  work.                                                                         
                                                                                
  Right now TARKAN learns:                                                      
                                                                                
  [                                                                             
  \text{aspect} \rightarrow \text{relevant evidence} \rightarrow                
  \text{polarity}.                                                              
  ]                                                                             
                                                                                
  But the teacher labels are still fundamentally **observational**:             
                                                                                
  > “this evidence is relevant/useful for this aspect.”                         
                                                                                
  I think the missing signal is:                                                
                                                                                
  > **“What happens to the prediction when this evidence is removed or          
  corrupted?”**                                                                 
                                                                                
  And you can create that supervision **without another backbone**.             
                                                                                
  ---                                                                           
                                                                                
  # The idea: Counterfactual Evidence Training (CET)                            
                                                                                
  For each training aspect (a), you already have:                               
                                                                                
  ```text                                                                       
  tweet                                                                         
  image                                                                         
  teacher-filtered KG                                                           
  aspect                                                                        
  gold polarity                                                                 
  ```                                                                           
                                                                                
  Construct several versions:                                                   
                                                                                
  ### Full                                                                      
                                                                                
  [                                                                             
  x^{full}=(tweet,image,KG)                                                     
  ]                                                                             
                                                                                
  ### Text-only                                                                 
                                                                                
  [                                                                             
  x^{text}=(tweet)                                                              
  ]                                                                             
                                                                                
  ### Visual-removed                                                            
                                                                                
  [                                                                             
  x^{-V}=(tweet,KG)                                                             
  ]                                                                             
                                                                                
  ### KG-removed                                                                
                                                                                
  [                                                                             
  x^{-G}=(tweet,image)                                                          
  ]                                                                             
                                                                                
  ### Corrupted evidence                                                        
                                                                                
  Replace the selected KG evidence with evidence from another aspect/tweet.     
                                                                                
  Then don't train the model only on the gold class.                            
                                                                                
  Train it on the **change in polarity evidence**.                              
                                                                                
  For example:                                                                  
                                                                                
  ```text FULL   → POS                                                          
  TEXT     → NEU                                                                
  ```                                                                           
                                                                                
  means:                                                                        
                                                                                
  > visual/KG evidence should cause a **POS shift**.                            
                                                                                
  Whereas:                                                                      
                                                                                
  ```text FULL   → POS                                                          
  TEXT     → POS                                                                
  ```                                                                           
                                                                                
  means:                                                                        
                                                                                
  > evidence should **preserve** POS rather than create a new direction.        
                                                                                
  This is **not PDS**. PDS asked a teacher to label direction. CET measures the 
  direction **from the student's own controlled interventions**.                
                                                                                
  ---                                                                           
                                                                                
  # The key loss                                                                
                                                                                
  Let (m(x)) be the student's polarity margin:                                  
                                                                                
  [                                                                             
  m(x)=z_{POS}-z_{NEG}                                                          
  ]                                                                             
                                                                                
  or more generally the gold-vs-best-alternative margin.                        
                                                                                
  Define the observed effect of evidence:                                       
                                                                                
  [                                                                             
  \Delta_V=m(x^{full})-m(x^{-V})                                                
  ]                                                                             
                                                                                
  [                                                                             
  \Delta_G=m(x^{full})-m(x^{-G}).                                               
  ]                                                                             
                                                                                
  Then use the teacher's relevance label to determine **which interventions     
  should matter**.                                                              
                                                                                
  If visual evidence is teacher-relevant:                                       
                                                                                
  [                                                                             
  L_V =                                                                         
  \max(0,\gamma-\operatorname{sign}(\Delta_V)\cdot|\Delta_V|)                   
  ]                                                                             
                                                                                
  If visual evidence is irrelevant:                                             
                                                                                
  [                                                                             
  L_V =                                                                         
  |\Delta_V|.                                                                   
  ]                                                                             
                                                                                
  Same for KG.                                                                  
                                                                                
  So TARKAN learns:                                                             
                                                                                
  > **Relevant evidence should change the target-specific decision; irrelevant  
  evidence should not.**                                                        
                                                                                
  That is much closer to the scientific claim of TARKAN than another polarity   
  head.                                                                         
                                                                                
  ---                                                                           
                                                                                
  # The really interesting part: **evidence swapping**                          
                                                                                
  This is the part I'd put my money on.                                         
                                                                                
  Suppose a tweet has:                                                          
                                                                                
  ```text                                                                       
  aspect A → POS                                                                
  aspect B → NEG                                                                
  ```                                                                           
                                                                                
  Your system has:                                                              
                                                                                
  ```text                                                                       
  E_A = evidence selected for A                                                 
  E_B = evidence selected for B                                                 
  ```                                                                           
                                                                                
  Create:                                                                       
                                                                                
  [                                                                             
  (A,E_A) \rightarrow POS                                                       
  ]                                                                             
                                                                                
  but deliberately train:                                                       
                                                                                
  [                                                                             
  (A,E_B) \rightarrow \text{NO-SHIFT / uncertainty}.                            
  ]                                                                             
                                                                                
  Likewise:                                                                     
                                                                                
  [                                                                             
  (B,E_A).                                                                      
  ]                                                                             
                                                                                
  This teaches the model:                                                       
                                                                                
  > **evidence belongs to an aspect, not merely to the tweet.**                 
                                                                                
  That's a missing inductive bias in the current architecture.                  
                                                                                
  And it directly targets the thing your POS/NEG→NEU errors are suggesting:     
  **the model often knows the tweet's sentiment but fails to isolate the        
  target-specific sentiment.**                                                  
                                                                                
  You tried sibling **logit** losses and sibling **input marking**. Those were  
  weak/negative. This is different:                                             
                                                                                
  **we corrupt the evidence–aspect binding itself.**                            
                                                                                
  ---                                                                           
                                                                                
  # Why I think this is more promising than another polarity architecture       
                                                                                
  Your latest results show:                                                     
                                                                                
  ```text polarity head changes → flat/negative                                 
  ```

  ```text id="qfrn6v"                                                           
  aspect

  what evidence actually belongs to this aspect?

  ```                                                                           
                                                                                
  You have repeatedly changed the second arrow.                                 
                                                                                
  **CET attacks the first arrow.**                                              
                                                                                
  It also uses a signal you already possess:

  * multiple aspects per tweet

  No new model family.
